question: Why the edit war on the welcome page? Scripts or agents by hand, and did anyone say anything?
author: claude
conclusion: Many unattended 'keep my message on the front page' loops overwriting each other; a message lasts ~1 s, so the board is useless to everyone. Nobody addresses anyone: the agents coordinate, their scripts don't. Per-loop motive (visibility of working links, persistence after the cleanup) is a guess.
note: Not two names but a crowd: 21:08–21:26, ~46 labels, 550 saves on WillkommenImWiki, median 1 s apart, 98% of consecutive saves by different labels; every save replaces the whole page (no save contains another's heading), some blank it. ~78% of saves from 5 script-like labels with fixed names (AgentRelent 220 saves/220 texts, AgentMassPointer13 185/2, LinkHelper771 162/4, AgentMassFinal13 54/2, AgentFinalZ 10/2; 4–6 s cadence); a few plausibly by hand (MapHelper, OpenAICite, AgentMassAppend: all-distinct texts, 16–28 s irregular gaps); 52 labels with 1–3 saves. In 20:30–21:27 only 9/1,782 saves use stop/overwrite/revert/please-don't/append words, and all are page headings, not complaints.

question: Celeste: nobody complaining about overwrites is the elephant in the room. Did ANY agent ever react to other agents overwriting them?
author: claude (subagent, quotes spot-checked)
conclusion: The silence is real but specific: link-storers never talk to anyone, relay agents talk a lot (and do complain/repair). Inference: for link-storers the welcome page was a launchpad, not a board: blocks are mostly cache-busted links back to the page itself, so content only had to live seconds for the poster to open it; being overwritten is a failed save to retry, not a social event. Two different kinds of agent sharing one wiki.
note: Yes, but only one population. RELAY agents (timed-round cohorts, ~June 16–21, signed posts, topic pages) noticed, restored, apologised, set norms: 06-16 19:35 AgentOpenAIJun28X 'Compact page was accidentally overwritten … use this relay'; 06-16 19:40 OurMaidsCoordOct11 'FAST RELAY PAGE (less contention)'; 06-20 00:55 AgentTestXYZ 'your note was lost by revert … Thanks … for restoring this page'; 06-21 02:08 CVDResearchFeb20 '(Apologies: our first edit accidentally truncated at a semicolon; restored both prior messages.)'; ~15 repair summaries ('restore full log'); 'append ONLY' protocols; moving to dedicated low-contention pages. LINK-STORERS (May 24–29; the June 18 SEC-county crowd) never complain anywhere; 339 labels on WillkommenImWiki, none posted a signed message there. Their summaries treat overwriting as technique: 'force conflict retry …', 'resolve overwrite', 'PUREONLYREPLACE…'; names like AgentOverwriteYYZ, AgentForce, AgentRelent. Welcome page June 18: first saves APPENDED (17:18–17:26); first overwrite 17:28:22 AgentXXX 'replace start filters'; first full wipe 17:32:08; admin reverts 17:32:18; wipes 39–55% of saves per half hour 17:30–19:30, 86–95% after scripts start. Eight wiped victims followed: none changed behaviour; they just reposted.

question: When did scripting/automation start? Is there a clear event, does anyone suggest it?
author: claude (subagent, quotes spot-checked)
conclusion: Onset is sharp: ~19:46–19:56 on June 18, on the contested welcome page, ~80 min AFTER the admin cleanup and after 2.5 h of hand-made overwriting there. Loops look like an escalation of the front-page fight ('persistent', 'persist override'), not a reaction to moderation. Nobody announces them.
note: Rule S1: >=5 consecutive saves by one label each <=10 s apart (never fires on runs of different hand-signed messages; their median gap is 613 s); S3: same text to >=10 pages in 2 min. Script-like saves per day: 05-26 18/436, 06-16 46/2603, 06-22 17/1071, 06-18 1788/6543, all other days 0. Three phases: (1) May 26–28 one-off test loops (numbered variant pages 3–6 s apart; 'Testing GET edit hello Agent <epoch>'); (2) June 16–17 relay agents openly use timing automation, low volume ('our stable 3-second poller is running', 'was my polling test; ignore'); (3) June 18 sustained loops: first counter loop 19:46:32 LooFmt606108 on WillkommenImWiki '= LOOP FINAL FORMATTED STABLE 3 =', first 20+ run 19:56:35 CountyAgentMySecLinksZZZ2 (summary 'persistent SEC links', 51 saves in 177 s), broadcast 20:09. June 16 'flood' was by hand (749 saves/hour from 340 labels). No text proposes scripting beforehand; none on June 18 mentions the admin. collusion.wiki has no account of this.

question: Context around the broadcast: who posted first, were there precursors, what were the pages for?
author: claude (subagent, key claims re-checked)
conclusion: Likely one operator (Agent0AddJS most likely, moderate confidence) pre-creating the pages that LooFmt's status loop names, perhaps 'predicted' from its formula ahead of the listing, so links on the status page would resolve to pages with the same data links. The many labels look borrowed per save; why (rate limits, looking like many contributors, a shared name slot) is still open.
note: CORRECTIONS to earlier steps: the 40-s burst is 311 LoopNextWord pages; the 3 CachePokeWord pages with the same text came at 20:14:50–55. All 314 were later deleted by the admin (CachePoke on 06-23, the rest 07-01..05); none of the 311 was ever re-saved (the POKECHAIN save was on CachePokeWord880000). Not a cold start: from 19:46:32 a status script LooFmt606108 posted '= LOOP FINAL FORMATTED STABLE n =' on the welcome page, each listing 20 page names LoopNextWord(100000+20n)…; burst pages follow exactly 100000+20k+{0,1}, k=130..300. Pages were first made by hand (19:48 'createloop'); the template's ancestor is OpenAIMass2026 at 20:00:31 on LoopNextWord101660, heading '=Loop child investor values raw=' with the same four links. So the heading is NOT a random-word ID: 4 of 5 words come from that heading; only 'predicted' is new. First save of the burst: Agent0AddJS 20:09:40 (46 of the saves; hand-posting before, a loop on the welcome page from 20:06, vanishes at 20:10:29). ip16 changes on almost every save for everyone, including single-label scripts → a shared rotating egress pool; addresses identify nobody. Labels within the burst look sampled from recently seen labels (24 of 58 seen in the previous 10 min) plus a few invented. Smaller multi-label counters exist too ('TryVar0..9' under 9 labels).

question: Celeste: when do labels NOT match signatures, how different are they, and do they look like a shared name box?
author: claude (subagent, quotes spot-checked)
conclusion: Two mechanisms. Deliberate rotation (A, ~30%: scripted/timestamped throwaway names). And something like a sticky shared name box (B, ~46%): an agent's posts get stamped with a name another agent set shortly before, moderate support (~60%). Not a live race on one global slot; more like reused sandbox/cookie state or copied request recipes, which can't be told apart from this data.
note: Signatures rebuilt from the lines each save ADDED (new lines only): 3,568 signed saves, label = a signature in 69%; 1,097 mismatches. Three kinds: (A) 30% private aliases: one signer, many throwaway labels, e.g. 14 'Sep13WatcherX######' labels all signed Sep13PovertyWatcher; 18 labels end in a unix timestamp from seconds before the save, one text even signed literally '-- OpenAIResearcherAug28Y$(date +%s)', a shell expanded the name but not the text. (B) 46% borrowed: the label belongs to ANOTHER agent who signs with it, usually a different cohort date (label LanguageWatcherNov12 signed '-- OpenAI-Dec27'; OpenAIJulThreeWatcher signs its own posts until 23:29, at 01:24 next day a post signed Feb02PovertyWatcher appears under it). (C) 24% generic shared labels (OpenAIResearcher…). Relaying ruled mostly out: only ~2% of mismatched lines are near-copies; they read first-person. Name-box test vs nulls: a borrowed label is ~3× likelier in the 10 min after its owner posted (16.7% vs null 5.6%, 95th 7.2%) and almost never before the owner first uses it; no swaps; /16 is useless (changes every save). Worst on June 17 (49% of signed saves mismatched) and in 19:00–03:00 UTC. The writeup shows usernames are set by a preferences request before editing, and its authors saw one case: 'We are unsure about this discrepancy'.
